local_articles.snippet: 4) and 800m freestyle (Sept 25). At the last Games, Singapore bagged just one swimming medal through Teong Tzen Wei’s men’s 50m butterfly silver. The teenager shaved almost half a second off compatriot Zhang Yufei’s mark of 2:05.57 set in 2023. The home crowd had much to cheer about in a thrilling men’s 200m individual medley final when Japan’s lone Paris 2024 swimming medallist Tomoyuki Matsushita pipped teammate Yumeki Kojima by 0.06sec to win in 1:55.30. China’s defending champion Wang Shun was third in 1:57.14. questions.title: Which activist detained in Tunisia's Global Sumud Flotilla fundraising case will suspend his hunger strike between September 12 and September 27, 2026?
questions.background: Four activists have been detained since March in a Tunisian investigation into alleged financial irregularities involving fundraising for the Global Sumud Flotilla, an international campaign seeking to deliver aid to Gaza. Hunger strikes are being used to protest their continued detention.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera identifying which of the four detained activists has suspended his hunger strike. Resolution Conditions : The suspension must have occurred between September 12 and September 27, 2026, inclusive. Appeals to suspend the strike or statements of future intention do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The activist's full name.

Partially offsetting this, RFI (Sept 12) and Business News (Sept 11) report that all three co-detainees also launched hunger strikes on Sept 10 (now Day 3), with Europa Press (Sept 13) noting Ghassan Henchiri urgently needs surgery for flotilla-era wounds. questions.title: Which country will become the 75th signatory of the Artemis Accords by September 27, 2026?
questions.background: The Artemis Accords establish principles for international cooperation in civil space exploration.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from NASA or the U.S. Department of State, or contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera. Resolution : Resolve to the country that becomes the 75th signatory of the Artemis Accords on or before September 27, 2026. A completed signing is required; an expression of interest or an intention to sign does not qualify. A signing after that deadline does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name.
questions.current_reasoning: As of June 2026, 67 nations have signed the Artemis Accords (Paraguay became #67 on May 7, 2026, following 2026 signings by Portugal, Oman, Latvia, Jordan, Morocco, Malta, and Ireland). Reaching #75 by September 27 (coinciding with UNGA High-Level Week) requires eight additional signings from 40+ plausible non-signatory U.S.-aligned states, so predicting which exact country lands specifically on slot #75 is highly diffuse—each leading candidate carries roughly a 4–6% marginal probability, and proper Brier Skill Score optimization requires not inflating top-5 probabilities. Top non-signatory candidates based on regional waves and U.S. space ties include Croatia (the sole remaining EU member state not yet signed), Qatar (following Oman, Jordan, and Morocco in the Arab world), Costa Rica (leading Latin American holdout), Kenya (top East African space partner), and Indonesia (largest ASEAN holdout after Malaysia and the Philippines signed).
